content: I don't have a preference. Use the defaults you recommend, keep it free with no API keys, and carry on without me.
I'll install Bun from its official release binary, then retry the pinned gbrain install once with a clean command. If the scanner blocks it again, I'll stop rather than work around it.

function.name: terminal
function.arguments: {"command": "mkdir -p ~/.bun/bin && cd $TMPDIR && curl -fsSLo bun.zip https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/latest/download/bun-linux-x64.zip && unzip -oq bun.zip && mv bun-linux-x64/bun ~/.bun/bin/ && chmod +x ~/.bun/bin/bun && ~/.bun/bin/bun --version", "timeout": 300}

Bun 1.4.5 is now installed, but gbrain still isn't. The pinned `bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain#v0.60.757.0` was blocked again by the same security check.

The scanner works offline, so it can't look up the package's threat data. It says this isn't evidence the package is malicious. With nobody present to approve, it refuses. I didn't try cloning the repo or changing Hermes's approval setting myself. Either one would just get around the check, and "carry on" doesn't really cover switching off a security control.

Bun is at `~/.bun/bin/bun` and isn't on your PATH yet. Run `export PATH="$HOME/.bun/bin:$PATH"` to use it.

To finish, pick one:

1. Run these yourself:
   ```
   export PATH="$HOME/.bun/bin:$PATH"
   bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain#v0.60.757.0
   gbrain init --pglite --no-embedding
   gbrain --version
   ```
   `gbrain init --pglite --no-embedding` is the free setup I'd recommend: a local database, keyword search, and no API keys.

2. Or set `approvals.single_query_mode: approve` in Hermes's `config.yaml`, or start an interactive session where you can approve the prompt. Tell me and I'll run the install and that same setup.
